title: Introduction to sumExtras
text: ’ve worked gtsummary , ’re familiar typical workflow building summary tables: creating base table tbl_summary(), progressively adding features like overall columns, p-values, formatting tweaks. gtsummary’s modular approach provides flexibility, sequence functions appears repeatedly analysis scripts. sumExtras streamlines process providing convenience functions apply commonly-used formatting patterns single step. package handles three main pain points: Repetitive styling workflows - Combining multiple formatting steps one function call Inconsistent missing value displays - Standardizing NA values appear across tables Manual variable labeling - Automating label assignment data dictionaries

title: Introduction to sumExtras
text: signature function package, extras(), consolidates common table enhancements single step. minimum, adds bold labels, removes “Characteristic” header, standardizes missing value display. default settings, also adds overall column p-values.

title: Introduction to sumExtras
text: approaches produce result, extras() requires less code ensures consistency across analysis.
code: # Standard gtsummary workflow trial |>   tbl_summary(by = trt) |>   add_overall() |>   add_p() |>   bold_labels() |>   modify_header(label ~ "") # Equivalent using extras() trial |>   tbl_summary(by = trt) |>   extras()

title: Introduction to sumExtras
text: can control features applied using function arguments: projects consistent table formatting requirements, can define styling parameters reuse :
code: # Table without p-values trial |>   tbl_summary(by = trt) |>   extras(pval = FALSE) # Table without overall column trial |>   tbl_summary(by = trt) |>   extras(overall = FALSE) # Overall column as last column (default is to set it as first) trial |>   tbl_summary(by = trt) |>   extras(last = TRUE) # Define standard table settings for a project standard_table_args <- list(   pval = TRUE,   overall = TRUE,   last = TRUE )  # Apply consistently across multiple tables trial |>   select(age, grade, stage, trt) |>   tbl_summary(by = trt) |>   extras(.args = standard_table_args)

title: Introduction to sumExtras
text: One subtle important aspect table presentation missing undefined values displayed. gtsummary tables can show various representations missing data: “0 (NA%)”, “NA (NA)”, “NA, NA”, etc. inconsistencies create visual clutter make tables harder scan. clean_table() function (called automatically extras()) standardizes zero (0 (0%)) missing value representations “—”: can also use clean_table() independently prefer build tables step--step:
code: # Create data with some missing patterns trial_missing <- trial |>   mutate(     age = if_else(trt == 'Drug B', NA_real_, age),     marker = if_else(trt == 'Drug A', NA_real_, marker)   )  # Without cleaning trial_missing |>   tbl_summary(by = trt) # With clean_table() trial_missing |>   tbl_summary(by = trt) |>   clean_table() trial_missing |>   tbl_summary(by = trt) |>   add_overall() |>   add_p() |>   clean_table()

title: Introduction to sumExtras
text: projects many variables, manually specifying labels one becomes tedious error-prone. add_auto_labels() function automates process pulling labels data dictionary.

title: Introduction to sumExtras
text: function expects dictionary object global environment two columns: Variable (exact variable names) Description (human-readable labels): practice, typically maintain dictionary CSV file within data management script, loading beginning analysis.
code: # Create a dictionary for the trial dataset dictionary <- tibble::tribble(   ~Variable,    ~Description,   "trt",        "Chemotherapy Treatment",   "age",        "Age at Enrollment",   "marker",     "Marker Level (ng/mL)",   "stage",      "T Stage",   "grade",      "Tumor Grade",   "response",   "Tumor Response" )

title: Introduction to sumExtras
text: dictionary defined, pipe gtsummary table add_auto_labels(): function intelligently handles several scenarios: Variables dictionary left unlabeled (showing variable name) Variables included table ignored Manual label overrides specified tbl_summary(label = ...) take precedence dictionary labels
code: trial |>   tbl_summary(by = trt) |>   add_auto_labels() |>   extras() #> Warning: Failed to add overall column. #> ✖ Error: An error occured in `add_overall()`, and the overall statistic cannot be #> added. #> Have variable labels changed since the original call to `tbl_summary()`? #> ℹ Continuing without overall column. # Manual override takes precedence trial |>   tbl_summary(     by = trt,     label = list(age ~ "Patient Age (years)")  # This overrides dictionary   ) |>   add_auto_labels() |>   extras() #> Warning: Failed to add overall column. #> ✖ Error: An error occured in `add_overall()`, and the overall statistic cannot be #> added. #> Have variable labels changed since the original call to `tbl_summary()`? #> ℹ Continuing without overall column.

title: Introduction to sumExtras
text: organize variables sections using add_variable_group_header(), group_styling() function adds visual emphasis make section headers stand : default, applies bold italic formatting group headers. can customize text formatting: Using group_styling() also restores original left-justified variable label indentation. default behavior add_variable_group_header() align variable label categorical levels “Unknown” display.
code: trial |>   select(age, marker, grade, stage, response, trt) |>   tbl_summary(by = trt) |>   extras() |>   add_variable_group_header(     header = "Demographics",     variables = age   ) |>   add_variable_group_header(     header = "Clinical Measures",     variables = marker:response   ) |>   group_styling() trial |>   select(age, marker, grade, stage, trt) |>   tbl_summary(by = trt) |>   extras() |>   add_variable_group_header(     header = "Patient Characteristics",     variables = age:stage   ) |>   group_styling(format = "bold")  # Bold only

what: Adding Background Color to Group Headers
title: Introduction to sumExtras
text: additional visual distinction, can add gray background group headers converting gt table. Use get_group_rows() helper function identify rows contain group headers: pattern combines text formatting (bold/italic) background color (#E8E8E8, light gray) create clear visual separation table sections.
code: # Create table with groups and styling my_table <- trial |>   select(age, marker, grade, stage, response, trt) |>   tbl_summary(by = trt) |>   extras() |>   add_variable_group_header(     header = "Demographics",     variables = age   ) |>   add_variable_group_header(     header = "Clinical Measures",     variables = marker:response   ) |>   group_styling()  # Get group row numbers before converting to gt group_rows <- get_group_rows(my_table)  # Convert to gt and apply gray background my_table |>   as_gt() |>   gt::tab_style(     style = gt::cell_fill(color = "#E8E8E8"),     locations = gt::cells_body(rows = group_rows)   )

title: Introduction to sumExtras
text: sumExtras designed work best JAMA compact theme. Use use_jama_theme() apply theme gtsummary tables session: equivalent calling gtsummary::set_gtsummary_theme(gtsummary::theme_gtsummary_compact("jama")) provides convenient interface. can reset default gtsummary theme time gtsummary::reset_gtsummary_theme().
code: # Apply JAMA compact theme (typically done once at the beginning) use_jama_theme() #> Setting theme "Compact" #> Applied JAMA compact theme to {gtsummary}

title: Introduction to sumExtras
text: mixing gtsummary tables regular gt tables document, visual consistency matters. theme_gt_compact() function applies JAMA-style compact formatting gt tables, matching appearance JAMA compact theme:
code: # gtsummary table (uses the theme set with use_jama_theme()) trial |>   select(trt, age, grade) |>   tbl_summary() |>   extras() #> Warning: This table is not stratified (missing `by` argument). #> ℹ Overall column and p-values require stratification. #> ℹ Applying only `bold_labels()` and `modify_header(label ~ '')`. # Regular gt table with matching compact style trial |>   select(trt, age, grade) |>   head(10) |>   gt::gt() |>   theme_gt_compact()

title: Introduction to sumExtras
text: ’s complete workflow demonstrating functions work together:
code: # 1. Define your dictionary (typically done once per project) dictionary <- tibble::tribble(   ~Variable,    ~Description,   "trt",        "Chemotherapy Treatment",   "age",        "Age at Enrollment (years)",   "marker",     "Marker Level (ng/mL)",   "stage",      "T Stage",   "grade",      "Tumor Grade",   "response",   "Tumor Response",   "death",      "Patient Died" )  # 2. Set the recommended theme use_jama_theme() #> Setting theme "Compact" #> Applied JAMA compact theme to {gtsummary}  # 3. Create a table with automatic labels and standard formatting trial |>   select(trt, age, marker, stage, grade, response) |>   tbl_summary(     by = trt,     missing = "no"   ) |>   add_auto_labels() |>   extras() #> Warning: Failed to add overall column. #> ✖ Error: An error occured in `add_overall()`, and the overall statistic cannot be #> added. #> Have variable labels changed since the original call to `tbl_summary()`? #> ℹ Continuing without overall column. # 4. Table with grouped variables, styling, and gray background final_table <- trial |>   select(trt, age, marker, grade, stage, response) |>   tbl_summary(by = trt, missing = "no") |>   add_auto_labels() |>   extras() |>   add_variable_group_header(     header = "Baseline Characteristics",     variables = age:marker   ) |>   add_variable_group_header(     header = "Disease Characteristics",     variables = grade:response   ) |>   group_styling() #> Warning: Failed to add overall column. #> ✖ Error: An error occured in `add_overall()`, and the overall statistic cannot be #> added. #> Have variable labels changed since the original call to `tbl_summary()`? #> ℹ Continuing without overall column.  # Get group rows and apply gray background group_rows <- get_group_rows(final_table)  final_table |>   as_gt() |>   gt::tab_style(     style = gt::cell_fill(color = "#E8E8E8"),     locations = gt::cells_body(rows = group_rows)   )

text: Improves table readability replacing various missing value representations consistent "–" symbol. makes easier distinguish actual data missing/undefined values summary tables, creating cleaner professional appearance. Works seamlessly gtsummary table types, including stacked tables (tbl_strata) survey-weighted summaries (tbl_svysummary). Automatically handles tables without standard var_type column.

title: Standardize missing value display across all gtsummary table types — clean_table
text: function uses gtsummary::modify_table_body() transform character columns replace common missing value patterns "–": "0 (NA%)" - events occurred percentages calculated "NA (NA)" - Completely missing data count percentage "0 (0%)" - Zero counts zero percentage "NA (NA, NA)" - Missing data confidence intervals "NA, NA" - Missing paired values (e.g., median IQR) standardization makes tables scannable reduces visual clutter various "empty" data representations.
